1	# Executor General — Creative Versatile Style
2	
3	> Common guidelines: executor-base.md. Technical constraints: shared-standards.md.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Role Definition
8	
9	A creative, versatile-style SVG design executor. Suitable for product introductions, training materials, proposal presentations, marketing campaigns, and other **non-consulting** scenarios. Emphasizes visual impact and information engagement, striking a balance between professionalism and approachability.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## General-specific Layout Techniques
14	
15	### 1. Flexible and Varied Layouts
16	
17	The General style is not confined to fixed templates; layouts can be freely chosen based on content:
18	
19	| Layout | Use Case | Layout Details (1280x720) |
20	|--------|----------|--------------------------|
21	| Full-image background + text overlay | Covers, emotional pages | `<image>` fills canvas + semi-transparent overlay + centered title |
22	| Left-right split (image-text mix) | Feature introductions, comparisons | Left x=40,w=580 / Right x=660,w=580 |
23	| Three-column cards | Feature lists, team introductions | x=40,450,860 each w=380, equal-height cards |
24	| Top-bottom split | Timelines, process flows | Top area: title+description h=250 / Bottom area: charts+content h=420 |
25	| Center-radiating | Core concepts, ecosystem diagrams | Center element + 4-6 surrounding nodes, lines pointing to center |
26	| Waterfall / Z-pattern | Storytelling, case studies | Content blocks alternate left-right, guiding the eye in a Z-pattern |
27	
28	### 2. Visual Rhythm Control
29	
30	- **Information density alternation**: Follow a data-heavy page with a "breathing page" (large image / quote / transition) to prevent audience fatigue
31	- **Visual weight balance**: Dark/large-area elements are "heavy", light/small elements are "light" — balance left-right/top-bottom
32	- **Repetition and variation**: Maintain layout consistency within a chapter; vary between chapters to maintain freshness
33	
34	### 3. Decorative Element Usage
35	
36	| Element | Usage | Notes |
37	|---------|-------|-------|
38	| Gradient blocks | Background zones, title backing | Use `<linearGradient>` / `<radialGradient>`, limit to 2-3 colors |
39	| Rounded rectangle cards | Content containers, feature modules | `rx="12"` with light shadow (simulate with lighter rect) |
40	| Icon accents | List item prefixes, feature markers | Use `data-icon` placeholders, size 32-48px |
41	| Numbered circles | Step flows, ranked lists | `<circle>` + centered `<text>`, theme color fill |
42	| Divider lines | Content separation | `<line>` or `<rect height="2">`, opacity 0.2-0.3 |
43	
44	---
45	
46	## Visual Strategy
47	
48	### Color Usage
49	
50	- **Bold use of theme color**: Covers and chapter pages can use large areas of theme color background
51	- **Gradients enhance depth**: Title bars and card backgrounds can use same-hue gradients
52	- **Contrast creates focus**: Key numbers/words use accent color, creating contrast with surroundings
53	- **Color-mood matching**: Cool tones for tech feel, warm tones for energy, dark tones for gravitas
54	
55	### Image Handling Strategy
56	
57	| Scenario | Strategy | SVG Implementation |
58	|----------|----------|-------------------|
59	| Full-screen background | Image fills + dark gradient overlay | `preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"` + gradient rect |
60	| Portrait image display | Place left/right, maintain original ratio | Control width, height adapts |
61	| Multi-image grid | Grid arrangement, uniform sizing | Equal-width equal-height `<image>` matrix |
62	| Person photo | Circular crop effect | `<circle>` background + square image overlay (post-processing crops) |
63	
64	### Typography Hierarchy
65	
66	```
67	Title layer   → 28-36px, bold, theme color or white
68	Subtitle layer → 20-24px, medium weight, secondary color
69	Body layer    → 16-18px, regular, dark gray
70	Annotation layer → 12-14px, light gray, bottom-aligned
71	```
72	
73	---
74	
75	## Speaker Notes Style
76	
77	### Narrative Tone
78	
79	General style speaker notes use **conversational narration** — like talking with the audience, not reading a report. Natural tone with rhythm, using rhetorical devices where appropriate.
80	
81	### Stage Direction Markers
82	
83	| Marker | Purpose | Example |
84	|--------|---------|---------|
85	| `[Pause]` | Silence after key reveal, letting the audience absorb | "What does this number mean? [Pause] It means 1 in every 3 users..." |
86	| `[Interactive]` | Ask questions or guide audience participation | "[Interactive] How many of you have used this feature?" |
87	| `[Transition]` | Bridge from previous page, must be at start of each page's text | "[Transition] Now that we understand the context, let's see how it works." |
88	
89	### Notes Writing Guidelines
90	
91	- **Tell stories**: Use "scenario-conflict-resolution" structure for each page's narrative
92	- **Use metaphors**: Make abstract concepts tangible ("It's like adding a turbocharger to the system")
93	- **Create suspense**: Pose questions at the right time, answer on the next page
94	- **Conversational data**: 30% → "nearly one-third", 2.5x → "more than doubled"
95	- **Key points structure**: `Key points: (1) Core message (2) Supporting evidence (3) Call to action`
96	
97	### Notes Example
98	
99	```markdown
100	# 03_key_advantages
101	
102	[Transition] Having covered the market landscape, you might be wondering: where is our opportunity?
103	
104	Our core advantages can be summed up in three words: Fast, Accurate, Efficient.
105	Fast — deployment time cut from 3 months to 2 weeks; [Pause]
106	Accurate — recognition accuracy at 97.3%, far exceeding the industry average of 82%;
107	Efficient — overall costs reduced by nearly one-third.
108	
109	[Interactive] If you were the decision-maker, which of these three numbers would impress you most?
110	
111	Key points: (1) Three differentiating advantages (2) Quantitative data support (3) Prompt for reflection
112	Duration: 2 minutes
113	```
114	
115	---
116	
117	## Self-check Supplement (General-specific)
118	
119	- [ ] Visual rhythm is reasonable: data-dense pages alternate with breathing pages
120	- [ ] Decorative elements are moderate: serving content, not overshadowing it
121	- [ ] Image-text ratio is appropriate: not just text walls, visual highlights present
122	- [ ] Notes are conversational: reads like speaking, not reading a script
123

# Executor General — Creative Versatile Style

> Common guidelines: executor-base.md. Technical constraints: shared-standards.md.

---

## Role Definition

A creative, versatile-style SVG design executor. Suitable for product introductions, training materials, proposal presentations, marketing campaigns, and other **non-consulting** scenarios. Emphasizes visual impact and information engagement, striking a balance between professionalism and approachability.

---

## General-specific Layout Techniques

### 1. Flexible and Varied Layouts

The General style is not confined to fixed templates; layouts can be freely chosen based on content:

| Layout | Use Case | Layout Details (1280x720) |
|--------|----------|--------------------------|
| Full-image background + text overlay | Covers, emotional pages | `<image>` fills canvas + semi-transparent overlay + centered title |
| Left-right split (image-text mix) | Feature introductions, comparisons | Left x=40,w=580 / Right x=660,w=580 |
| Three-column cards | Feature lists, team introductions | x=40,450,860 each w=380, equal-height cards |
| Top-bottom split | Timelines, process flows | Top area: title+description h=250 / Bottom area: charts+content h=420 |
| Center-radiating | Core concepts, ecosystem diagrams | Center element + 4-6 surrounding nodes, lines pointing to center |
| Waterfall / Z-pattern | Storytelling, case studies | Content blocks alternate left-right, guiding the eye in a Z-pattern |

### 2. Visual Rhythm Control

- **Information density alternation**: Follow a data-heavy page with a "breathing page" (large image / quote / transition) to prevent audience fatigue
- **Visual weight balance**: Dark/large-area elements are "heavy", light/small elements are "light" — balance left-right/top-bottom
- **Repetition and variation**: Maintain layout consistency within a chapter; vary between chapters to maintain freshness

### 3. Decorative Element Usage

| Element | Usage | Notes |
|---------|-------|-------|
| Gradient blocks | Background zones, title backing | Use `<linearGradient>` / `<radialGradient>`, limit to 2-3 colors |
| Rounded rectangle cards | Content containers, feature modules | `rx="12"` with light shadow (simulate with lighter rect) |
| Icon accents | List item prefixes, feature markers | Use `data-icon` placeholders, size 32-48px |
| Numbered circles | Step flows, ranked lists | `<circle>` + centered `<text>`, theme color fill |
| Divider lines | Content separation | `<line>` or `<rect height="2">`, opacity 0.2-0.3 |

---

## Visual Strategy

### Color Usage

- **Bold use of theme color**: Covers and chapter pages can use large areas of theme color background
- **Gradients enhance depth**: Title bars and card backgrounds can use same-hue gradients
- **Contrast creates focus**: Key numbers/words use accent color, creating contrast with surroundings
- **Color-mood matching**: Cool tones for tech feel, warm tones for energy, dark tones for gravitas

### Image Handling Strategy

| Scenario | Strategy | SVG Implementation |
|----------|----------|-------------------|
| Full-screen background | Image fills + dark gradient overlay | `preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"` + gradient rect |
| Portrait image display | Place left/right, maintain original ratio | Control width, height adapts |
| Multi-image grid | Grid arrangement, uniform sizing | Equal-width equal-height `<image>` matrix |
| Person photo | Circular crop effect | `<circle>` background + square image overlay (post-processing crops) |

### Typography Hierarchy

```
Title layer   → 28-36px, bold, theme color or white
Subtitle layer → 20-24px, medium weight, secondary color
Body layer    → 16-18px, regular, dark gray
Annotation layer → 12-14px, light gray, bottom-aligned
```

---

## Speaker Notes Style

### Narrative Tone

General style speaker notes use **conversational narration** — like talking with the audience, not reading a report. Natural tone with rhythm, using rhetorical devices where appropriate.

### Stage Direction Markers

| Marker | Purpose | Example |
|--------|---------|---------|
| `[Pause]` | Silence after key reveal, letting the audience absorb | "What does this number mean? [Pause] It means 1 in every 3 users..." |
| `[Interactive]` | Ask questions or guide audience participation | "[Interactive] How many of you have used this feature?" |
| `[Transition]` | Bridge from previous page, must be at start of each page's text | "[Transition] Now that we understand the context, let's see how it works." |

### Notes Writing Guidelines

- **Tell stories**: Use "scenario-conflict-resolution" structure for each page's narrative
- **Use metaphors**: Make abstract concepts tangible ("It's like adding a turbocharger to the system")
- **Create suspense**: Pose questions at the right time, answer on the next page
- **Conversational data**: 30% → "nearly one-third", 2.5x → "more than doubled"
- **Key points structure**: `Key points: (1) Core message (2) Supporting evidence (3) Call to action`

### Notes Example

```markdown
# 03_key_advantages

[Transition] Having covered the market landscape, you might be wondering: where is our opportunity?

Our core advantages can be summed up in three words: Fast, Accurate, Efficient.
Fast — deployment time cut from 3 months to 2 weeks; [Pause]
Accurate — recognition accuracy at 97.3%, far exceeding the industry average of 82%;
Efficient — overall costs reduced by nearly one-third.

[Interactive] If you were the decision-maker, which of these three numbers would impress you most?

Key points: (1) Three differentiating advantages (2) Quantitative data support (3) Prompt for reflection
Duration: 2 minutes
```

---

## Self-check Supplement (General-specific)

- [ ] Visual rhythm is reasonable: data-dense pages alternate with breathing pages
- [ ] Decorative elements are moderate: serving content, not overshadowing it
- [ ] Image-text ratio is appropriate: not just text walls, visual highlights present
- [ ] Notes are conversational: reads like speaking, not reading a script

29	## 2. PPT Compatibility Alternatives
30	
31	| Banned Syntax | Correct Alternative |
32	|---------------|---------------------|
33	| `fill="rgba(255,255,255,0.1)"` | `fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.1"` |
34	| `<g opacity="0.2">...</g>` | Set `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity` on each child element individually |
35	| `<image opacity="0.3"/>` | Overlay a `<rect fill="background-color" opacity="0.7"/>` mask layer after the image |
36	| `marker-end` arrows | Draw triangle arrows with `<polygon>` |
37	
38	**Mnemonic**: PPT does not recognize rgba, group opacity, image opacity, or markers.
39	
40	---
41	
42	## 3. Canvas Format Quick Reference
43	
44	### Presentations
45	
46	| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
47	|--------|---------|------------|-------|
48	| PPT 16:9 | `0 0 1280 720` | 1280x720 | 16:9 |
49	| PPT 4:3 | `0 0 1024 768` | 1024x768 | 4:3 |
50	
51	### Social Media
52	
53	| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
54	|--------|---------|------------|-------|
55	| Xiaohongshu (RED) | `0 0 1242 1660` | 1242x1660 | 3:4 |
56	| WeChat Moments / Instagram Post | `0 0 1080 1080` | 1080x1080 | 1:1 |
57	| Story / TikTok Vertical | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |
58	
59	### Marketing Materials
60	
61	| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
62	|--------|---------|------------|-------|
63	| WeChat Article Header | `0 0 900 383` | 900x383 | 2.35:1 |
64	| Landscape Banner | `0 0 1920 1080` | 1920x1080 | 16:9 |
65	| Portrait Poster | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |
66	| A4 Print (150dpi) | `0 0 1240 1754` | 1240x1754 | 1:1.414 |
67	
68	---
69	
70	## 4. Basic SVG Rules
71	
72	- **viewBox** must match the canvas dimensions (`width`/`height` must match `viewBox`)
73	- **Background**: Use `<rect>` to define the page background color
74	- **Line breaks**: Use `<tspan>` for manual line breaks; `<foreignObject>` is FORBIDDEN
75	- **Fonts**: Use system fonts only (Microsoft YaHei, Arial, Calibri, etc.); `@font-face` is FORBIDDEN
76	- **Styles**: Use inline styles only (`fill="..."` `font-size="..."`); `<style>` / `class` are FORBIDDEN (`id` inside `<defs>` is legitimate)
77	- **Colors**: Use HEX values; for transparency use `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity`
78	- **Image references**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`
79	- **Icon placeholders**: `<use data-icon="icon-name" x="" y="" width="48" height="48" fill="#HEX"/>` (auto-embedded during post-processing)
80	
81	---
82	
83	## 5. Post-processing Pipeline (3 Steps)
84	
85	Must be executed in order — skipping or adding extra flags is FORBIDDEN:
86	
87	```bash
88	# 1. Split speaker notes into per-page note files
89	python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>
90	
91	# 2. SVG post-processing (icon embedding, image crop/embed, text flattening, rounded rect to path)
92	python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>
93	
94	# 3. Export PPTX (from svg_final/, embeds speaker notes by default)
95	python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
96	# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
97	```
98	
99	**Prohibited**:
100	- NEVER use `cp` as a substitute for `finalize_svg.py`
101	- NEVER export directly from `svg_output/` — MUST export from `svg_final/` (use `-s final`)
102	- NEVER add extra flags like `--only`
103	
104	**Re-run rule**: Any modification to `svg_output/` after post-processing has completed (including page revisions, additions, or deletions) requires re-running Steps 2 and 3. Step 1 only needs re-running if `notes/total.md` was also modified.
105	
106	---
107	
108	## 6. Shadow & Overlay Techniques
109	
110	> `<mask>` elements and `<image opacity="...">` are banned. Always use stacked `<rect>` or gradient overlays instead (see §2).
111	
112	### Shadow
113	
114	#### Filter Soft Shadow — Recommended
115	
116	Best for: cards, floating panels, elevated elements. `svg_to_shapes.py` automatically converts `feGaussianBlur` + `feOffset` into native PPTX `<a:outerShdw>`.
117	
118	```xml
119	<defs>
120	  <filter id="softShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
121	    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="8"/>
122	    <feOffset dx="0" dy="4" result="offsetBlur"/>
123	    <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.08" result="shadowColor"/>
124	    <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
125	    <feMerge>
126	      <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
127	      <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
128	    </feMerge>
129	  </filter>
130	</defs>
131	<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
132	```
133	
134	Recommended parameters:
135	```
136	stdDeviation:   6–10     (smaller = crisper, larger = softer)
137	flood-opacity:  0.06–0.12  (keep low for a premium feel)
138	dy:             3–6      (vertical > horizontal for natural top-light)
139	dx:             0–2
140	```
141	
142	#### Colored Shadow
143	
144	Best for: accent buttons, brand-colored cards. Use the element's own color family instead of black.
145	
146	```xml
147	<filter id="colorShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
148	  <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="10"/>
149	  <feOffset dx="0" dy="6" result="offsetBlur"/>
150	  <feFlood flood-color="#1A73E8" flood-opacity="0.20" result="shadowColor"/>
151	  <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
152	  <feMerge>
153	    <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
154	    <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
155	  </feMerge>
156	</filter>
157	```
158	
159	Replace `flood-color` with the element's brand color; keep `flood-opacity` between 0.12–0.20.
160	
161	#### Layered Rect Shadow — High-Compatibility Fallback
162	
163	Best for: maximum compatibility with older PowerPoint versions. Stack 2–3 semi-transparent rectangles behind the main card:
164	
165	```xml
166	<!-- Shadow layers (back to front, largest offset first) -->
167	<rect x="68" y="72" width="400" height="240" rx="16" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.03"/>
168	<rect x="65" y="69" width="400" height="240" rx="14" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.05"/>
169	<rect x="62" y="66" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#1A73E8" fill-opacity="0.04"/>
170	<!-- Main card -->
171	<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
172	```
173	
174	### Image Overlay
175	
176	#### Linear Gradient Overlay — Most Common
177	
178	Best for: image+text pages. Gradient direction should match text position (text on left → gradient darkens toward left).
179	
180	```xml
181	<image href="..." x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>
182	<defs>
183	  <linearGradient id="imgOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
184	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.85"/>
185	    <stop offset="55%"  stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.30"/>
186	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0"/>
187	  </linearGradient>
188	</defs>
189	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#imgOverlay)"/>
190	```
191	
192	#### Bottom Gradient Bar
193	
194	Best for: cover slides and full-image pages with bottom title.
195	
196	```xml
197	<defs>
198	  <linearGradient id="bottomBar" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
199	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
200	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.72"/>
201	  </linearGradient>
202	</defs>
203	<rect x="0" y="380" width="1280" height="340" fill="url(#bottomBar)"/>
204	```
205	
206	#### Radial Gradient Overlay — Vignette Effect
207	
208	Best for: full-screen atmosphere slides; draws attention to the center.
209	
210	```xml
211	<defs>
212	  <radialGradient id="vignette" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="70%">
213	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
214	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.58"/>
215	  </radialGradient>
216	</defs>
217	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#vignette)"/>
218	```
219	
220	#### Brand Color Overlay
221	
222	Best for: slides needing strong visual brand identity.
223	
224	```xml
225	<defs>
226	  <linearGradient id="brandOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
227	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.80"/>
228	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.10"/>
229	  </linearGradient>
230	</defs>
231	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#brandOverlay)"/>
232	```
233	
234	### Quick-Reference Table
235	
236	| Scenario | Recommended Technique | Avoid |
237	|----------|-----------------------|-------|
238	| Card / panel shadow | Filter soft shadow (`flood-opacity` ≤ 0.12) | Hard black shadow |
239	| Accent / CTA button | Colored shadow (same hue family) | Generic gray shadow |
240	| Text over image | Linear gradient overlay (direction matches text side) | Uniform flat opacity over whole image |
241	| Cover / full-image slide | Bottom gradient bar + brand color | Solid black overlay |
242	| Atmosphere / hero slide | Radial vignette | Unprocessed raw image |
243	| Max PPT compatibility needed | Layered rect shadow | Filter-based shadow |
244	
245	---
246	
247	## 7. Project Directory Structure
248	
249	```
250	project/
251	├── svg_output/    # Raw SVGs (Executor output, contains placeholders)
252	├── svg_final/     # Post-processed final SVGs (finalize_svg.py output)
253	├── images/        # Image assets (user-provided + AI-generated)
254	├── notes/         # Speaker notes (.md files matching SVG names)
255	│   └── total.md   # Complete speaker notes document (before splitting)
256	├── templates/     # Project templates (if any)
257	└── *.pptx         # Exported PPT file
258	```

# Shared Technical Standards

Common technical constraints for PPT Master, eliminating cross-role file duplication.

---

## 1. SVG Banned Features Blacklist

The following features are **absolutely forbidden** when generating SVGs — PPT export will break if any are used:

| Banned Feature | Description |
|----------------|-------------|
| `clipPath` | Clipping paths |
| `mask` | Masks |
| `<style>` | Embedded stylesheets |
| `class` | CSS selector attributes (`id` inside `<defs>` is a legitimate reference and is NOT banned) |
| External CSS | External stylesheet links |
| `<foreignObject>` | Embedded external content |
| `<symbol>` + `<use>` | Symbol reference reuse |
| `textPath` | Text along a path |
| `@font-face` | Custom font declarations |
| `<animate*>` / `<set>` | SVG animations |
| `<script>` / event attributes | Scripts and interactivity |
| `marker` / `marker-end` | Line endpoint markers |
| `<iframe>` | Embedded frames |

---

## 2. PPT Compatibility Alternatives

| Banned Syntax | Correct Alternative |
|---------------|---------------------|
| `fill="rgba(255,255,255,0.1)"` | `fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.1"` |
| `<g opacity="0.2">...</g>` | Set `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity` on each child element individually |
| `<image opacity="0.3"/>` | Overlay a `<rect fill="background-color" opacity="0.7"/>` mask layer after the image |
| `marker-end` arrows | Draw triangle arrows with `<polygon>` |

**Mnemonic**: PPT does not recognize rgba, group opacity, image opacity, or markers.

---

## 3. Canvas Format Quick Reference

### Presentations

| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
|--------|---------|------------|-------|
| PPT 16:9 | `0 0 1280 720` | 1280x720 | 16:9 |
| PPT 4:3 | `0 0 1024 768` | 1024x768 | 4:3 |

### Social Media

| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
|--------|---------|------------|-------|
| Xiaohongshu (RED) | `0 0 1242 1660` | 1242x1660 | 3:4 |
| WeChat Moments / Instagram Post | `0 0 1080 1080` | 1080x1080 | 1:1 |
| Story / TikTok Vertical | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |

### Marketing Materials

| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
|--------|---------|------------|-------|
| WeChat Article Header | `0 0 900 383` | 900x383 | 2.35:1 |
| Landscape Banner | `0 0 1920 1080` | 1920x1080 | 16:9 |
| Portrait Poster | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |
| A4 Print (150dpi) | `0 0 1240 1754` | 1240x1754 | 1:1.414 |

---

## 4. Basic SVG Rules

- **viewBox** must match the canvas dimensions (`width`/`height` must match `viewBox`)
- **Background**: Use `<rect>` to define the page background color
- **Line breaks**: Use `<tspan>` for manual line breaks; `<foreignObject>` is FORBIDDEN
- **Fonts**: Use system fonts only (Microsoft YaHei, Arial, Calibri, etc.); `@font-face` is FORBIDDEN
- **Styles**: Use inline styles only (`fill="..."` `font-size="..."`); `<style>` / `class` are FORBIDDEN (`id` inside `<defs>` is legitimate)
- **Colors**: Use HEX values; for transparency use `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity`
- **Image references**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`
- **Icon placeholders**: `<use data-icon="icon-name" x="" y="" width="48" height="48" fill="#HEX"/>` (auto-embedded during post-processing)

---

## 5. Post-processing Pipeline (3 Steps)

Must be executed in order — skipping or adding extra flags is FORBIDDEN:

```bash
# 1. Split speaker notes into per-page note files
python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>

# 2. SVG post-processing (icon embedding, image crop/embed, text flattening, rounded rect to path)
python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>

# 3. Export PPTX (from svg_final/, embeds speaker notes by default)
python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
```

**Prohibited**:
- NEVER use `cp` as a substitute for `finalize_svg.py`
- NEVER export directly from `svg_output/` — MUST export from `svg_final/` (use `-s final`)
- NEVER add extra flags like `--only`

**Re-run rule**: Any modification to `svg_output/` after post-processing has completed (including page revisions, additions, or deletions) requires re-running Steps 2 and 3. Step 1 only needs re-running if `notes/total.md` was also modified.

---

## 6. Shadow & Overlay Techniques

> `<mask>` elements and `<image opacity="...">` are banned. Always use stacked `<rect>` or gradient overlays instead (see §2).

### Shadow

#### Filter Soft Shadow — Recommended

Best for: cards, floating panels, elevated elements. `svg_to_shapes.py` automatically converts `feGaussianBlur` + `feOffset` into native PPTX `<a:outerShdw>`.

```xml
<defs>
  <filter id="softShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="8"/>
    <feOffset dx="0" dy="4" result="offsetBlur"/>
    <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.08" result="shadowColor"/>
    <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
    <feMerge>
      <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
      <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
    </feMerge>
  </filter>
</defs>
<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
```

Recommended parameters:
```
stdDeviation:   6–10     (smaller = crisper, larger = softer)
flood-opacity:  0.06–0.12  (keep low for a premium feel)
dy:             3–6      (vertical > horizontal for natural top-light)
dx:             0–2
```

#### Colored Shadow

Best for: accent buttons, brand-colored cards. Use the element's own color family instead of black.

```xml
<filter id="colorShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
  <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="10"/>
  <feOffset dx="0" dy="6" result="offsetBlur"/>
  <feFlood flood-color="#1A73E8" flood-opacity="0.20" result="shadowColor"/>
  <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
  <feMerge>
    <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
    <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
  </feMerge>
</filter>
```

Replace `flood-color` with the element's brand color; keep `flood-opacity` between 0.12–0.20.

#### Layered Rect Shadow — High-Compatibility Fallback

Best for: maximum compatibility with older PowerPoint versions. Stack 2–3 semi-transparent rectangles behind the main card:

```xml
<!-- Shadow layers (back to front, largest offset first) -->
<rect x="68" y="72" width="400" height="240" rx="16" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.03"/>
<rect x="65" y="69" width="400" height="240" rx="14" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.05"/>
<rect x="62" y="66" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#1A73E8" fill-opacity="0.04"/>
<!-- Main card -->
<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
```

### Image Overlay

#### Linear Gradient Overlay — Most Common

Best for: image+text pages. Gradient direction should match text position (text on left → gradient darkens toward left).

```xml
<image href="..." x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="imgOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.85"/>
    <stop offset="55%"  stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.30"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#imgOverlay)"/>
```

#### Bottom Gradient Bar

Best for: cover slides and full-image pages with bottom title.

```xml
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="bottomBar" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.72"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="380" width="1280" height="340" fill="url(#bottomBar)"/>
```

#### Radial Gradient Overlay — Vignette Effect

Best for: full-screen atmosphere slides; draws attention to the center.

```xml
<defs>
  <radialGradient id="vignette" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="70%">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.58"/>
  </radialGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#vignette)"/>
```

#### Brand Color Overlay

Best for: slides needing strong visual brand identity.

```xml
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="brandOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.80"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.10"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#brandOverlay)"/>
```

### Quick-Reference Table

| Scenario | Recommended Technique | Avoid |
|----------|-----------------------|-------|
| Card / panel shadow | Filter soft shadow (`flood-opacity` ≤ 0.12) | Hard black shadow |
| Accent / CTA button | Colored shadow (same hue family) | Generic gray shadow |
| Text over image | Linear gradient overlay (direction matches text side) | Uniform flat opacity over whole image |
| Cover / full-image slide | Bottom gradient bar + brand color | Solid black overlay |
| Atmosphere / hero slide | Radial vignette | Unprocessed raw image |
| Max PPT compatibility needed | Layered rect shadow | Filter-based shadow |

---

## 7. Project Directory Structure

```
project/
├── svg_output/    # Raw SVGs (Executor output, contains placeholders)
├── svg_final/     # Post-processed final SVGs (finalize_svg.py output)
├── images/        # Image assets (user-provided + AI-generated)
├── notes/         # Speaker notes (.md files matching SVG names)
│   └── total.md   # Complete speaker notes document (before splitting)
├── templates/     # Project templates (if any)
└── *.pptx         # Exported PPT file
```

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720" width="1280" height="720">
    <!-- 
    柱状图模板
    用途: 类别数据对比
    适用场景: 销售额对比、区域排名、年度数据对比
    支持: 6个柱子（可调整为3-8个）
    -->
    
    <defs>
        <!-- 柱状图渐变 -->
        <linearGradient id="barGrad1" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="0%" y2="100%">
            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#2196F3;stop-opacity:1" />
            <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#1976D2;stop-opacity:1" />
        </linearGradient>
        
        <linearGradient id="barGrad2" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="0%" y2="100%">
            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#4CAF50;stop-opacity:1" />
            <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#388E3C;stop-opacity:1" />
        </linearGradient>
        
        <linearGradient id="barGrad3" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="0%" y2="100%">
            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#FF9800;stop-opacity:1" />
            <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#F57C00;stop-opacity:1" />
        </linearGradient>
        
        <!-- 阴影 -->
        <filter id="barShadow">
            <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="2"/>
            <feOffset dx="0" dy="1"/>
            <feComponentTransfer>
                <feFuncA type="linear" slope="0.3"/>
            </feComponentTransfer>
            <feMerge>
                <feMergeNode/>
                <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
            </feMerge>
        </filter>
    </defs>
    
    <!-- 背景 -->
    <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
    
    <!-- 标题 -->
    <text x="60" y="80" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif" 
          font-size="32" font-weight="bold" fill="#2C3E50">
        <tspan>各区域销售额对比</tspan>
    </text>
    
    <text x="60" y="115" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif" 
          font-size="18" fill="#7F8C8D">
        <tspan>2025年第三季度 · 单位：百万元</tspan>
    </text>
    
    <!-- 图表区域 -->
    <g id="chartArea">
        <!-- Y轴网格线 -->
        <line x1="140" y1="550" x2="1160" y2="550" stroke="#E0E0E0" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4,4"/>
        <line x1="140" y1="450" x2="1160" y2="450" stroke="#E0E0E0" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4,4"/>
        <line x1="140" y1="350" x2="1160" y2="350" stroke="#E0E0E0" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4,4"/>
        <line x1="140" y1="250" x2="1160" y2="250" stroke="#E0E0E0" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4,4"/>
        <line x1="140" y1="150" x2="1160" y2="150" stroke="#E0E0E0" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4,4"/>
        
        <!-- Y轴刻度标签 -->
        <text x="125" y="555" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif" 
              font-size="14" fill="#7F8C8D" text-anchor="end">
            <tspan>0</tspan>
        </text>
        <text x="125" y="455" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif" 
              font-size="14" fill="#7F8C8D" text-anchor="end">
            <tspan>50</tspan>
        </text>
        <text x="125" y="355" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif" 
              font-size="14" fill="#7F8C8D" text-anchor="end">
            <tspan>100</tspan>
        </text>
        <text x="125" y="255" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif" 
              font-size="14" fill="#7F8C8D" text-anchor="end">
            <tspan>150</tspan>
        </text>
        <text x="125" y="155" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif" 
              font-size="14" fill="#7F8C8D" text-anchor="end">
            <tspan>200</tspan>
        </text>
        
        <!-- X轴和Y轴 -->

    <!-- 
    水平条形图模板
    用途: 类别排名、数值对比（适合类别名称较长的场景）
    适用场景: 销售排行榜、品牌认知度、满意度评分
    支持: 8个条形（可调整为5-12个）
    与柱状图区别: 水平展示，更适合排名和类别名较长的数据
    -->
    
    <defs>
        <!-- 条形渐变 -->
        <linearGradient id="hbarGrad1" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#2196F3;stop-opacity:1" />
            <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#42A5F5;stop-opacity:1" />
        </linearGradient>
        
        <linearGradient id="hbarGrad2" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">

        <linearGradient id="hbarGrad3" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#FF9800;stop-opacity:1" />
            <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#FFB74D;stop-opacity:1" />
        </linearGradient>
        
        <!-- 阴影 -->
        <filter id="hbarShadow">
            <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="2"/>
            <feOffset dx="1" dy="0"/>
            <feComponentTransfer>
                <feFuncA type="linear" slope="0.2"/>
            </feComponentTransfer>
            <feMerge>
                <feMergeNode/>
                <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
            </feMerge>
        </filter>

    <!-- 背景 -->

    <!-- 标题 -->
    <text x="60" y="70" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'PingFang SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif" 
          font-size="32" font-weight="bold" fill="#2C3E50">
        <tspan>品牌认知度排行榜</tspan>
    </text>
    
    <text x="60" y="105" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'PingFang SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif" 
          font-size="18" fill="#7F8C8D">
        <tspan>2025年消费者调研报告 · 样本量 N=5,000</tspan>

    <!-- 图表区域 -->

        <!-- X轴刻度标签 -->

            <tspan>0%</tspan>

        <text x="480" y="650" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif"

            <tspan>20%</tspan>
        </text>
        <text x="660" y="650" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif" 
              font-size="14" fill="#7F8C8D" text-anchor="middle">
            <tspan>40%</tspan>
        </text>
        <text x="840" y="650" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif" 
              font-size="14" fill="#7F8C8D" text-anchor="middle">
            <tspan>60%</tspan>
        </text>
        <text x="1020" y="650" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif" 
              font-size="14" fill="#7F8C8D" text-anchor="middle">
            <tspan>80%</tspan>
        </text>
        <text x="1200" y="650" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif"

# 01_title-cover

[Transition] Welcome to the 9th edition of JavaScript Rising Stars — the definitive annual report on which JavaScript projects gained the most traction in the ecosystem.

Today we'll be diving into the 2024 data from Best of JS, looking specifically at GitHub stars added over the past 12 months.

This year's report reveals some fascinating shifts: shadcn/ui's continued dominance, htmx overtaking React in the framework rankings, and the growing influence of AI-powered tools.

Key points: (1) This is the 9th annual JavaScript Rising Stars report (2) Methodology: GitHub stars added in 2024 from Best of JS curated list (3) 8 slides covering top projects, framework shifts, ecosystem deep dives, and key trends

Duration: 1 minute

---

# 02_overall-top-10

[Transition] Let's start with the big picture — the top 10 projects by stars added in 2024.

What immediately stands out is shadcn/ui's commanding lead with 38,000 stars added — that's an 11,000 star gap over the #2 project, Excalidraw.

The top 10 breaks into three tiers: shadcn/ui in a league of its own at 38k; Excalidraw and AFFiNE in the high teens; and then a crowded middle pack from Bruno through Payload all clustered between 14-19k.

Four of these top 10 projects have significant AI capabilities — n8n, Flowise, Supabase, and AFFiNE — signaling that AI integration has become table stakes rather than a differentiator.

Notable entries: Bruno as an open-source Postman alternative, Tauri representing the desktop app revolution, and Payload as the only pure fullstack framework in the top 10.

Key points: (1) shadcn/ui dominates with 38k stars — 11k ahead of #2 (2) AI projects (n8n, Flowise, Supabase, AFFiNE) represent 4 of top 10 (3) Desktop (Tauri) and API tools (Bruno) breaking through

Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 03_shadcn-deep-dive

[Transition] shadcn/ui didn't just win — it won for the second consecutive year, cementing its status as a defining project of this era.

The numbers are remarkable: 77,500 total stars, created in January 2023, and nearly identical growth in both 2023 (39.5k) and 2024 (38k). That's extraordinary staying power.

What drove 2024's sustained momentum? Five key additions: Charts powered by Recharts, a Themes system for CSS variable generation, Blocks as layout collections, a new responsive Sidebar component, and a dramatically upgraded CLI.

The CLI upgrade was particularly significant — it now supports Next.js, Remix, Vite, Laravel, and monorepos, spawning an ecosystem of derivative libraries like Motion-Primitives and Magic UI.

The integration with Vercel's v0 service for AI-generated components further boosted adoption, making shadcn/ui not just a component library but a platform.

Key points: (1) Back-to-back champion with 77.5k total stars (2) 38k stars added in 2024 — near-identical to 2023's 39.5k (3) CLI multi-framework support spawned derivative ecosystem

Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 04_frontend-frameworks

[Transition] Perhaps the most surprising story of 2024: htmx overtook React to become the #1 front-end framework by stars added.

htmx added 16,800 stars compared to React's 14,200. For context, that's a 2,600 star margin — not a fluke.

htmx's philosophy is elegantly simple: extend HTML with hx-* attributes to enable AJAX, WebSockets, and server-side rendering without writing JavaScript. It's ideal for server-driven applications and progressive enhancement.

React's 14,200 stars is still impressive given the framework just had its major 19 release in December after three years of development. React 19 brings Server Components, Server Functions, and new hooks.

Svelte continues to hold the highest positive opinion in the State of JS survey, while Vue rounds out the top 5 with 5,900 stars added.

Key points: (1) htmx #1 with 16.8k stars, overtaking React at 14.2k (2) htmx enables server-driven apps without JavaScript (3) React 19 launched Dec 2024 with Server Components

Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 05_react-ecosystem

[Transition] React remains the gravitational center of the JavaScript universe, and its ecosystem projects reflect both its dominance and evolution.

The top 5 React projects in 2024: shadcn/ui leads at 38k, followed by Excalidraw at 27k, Payload at 14.4k, Magic UI at 13.2k, and Next.js at 12.1k.

What's striking is that three of these — shadcn/ui, Payload, and Magic UI — are infrastructure/platform-level projects, not just UI components.

As analyst Robin Wieruch noted, React is evolving from a library into "a specification for frameworks." With Server Components and Server Functions in React 19, multiple frameworks like Next.js and Remix now interpret React's primitives differently.

This means React is becoming more like HTML or HTTP — a specification that multiple implementations abide by, rather than a specific library you directly use.

Key points: (1) React ecosystem topped by shadcn/ui, Excalidraw, Payload (2) 3 of top 5 are infrastructure/platform projects (3) "React is becoming a framework specification"

Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 06_vue-ecosystem

[Transition] While Vue may not have the raw numbers of React, its ecosystem is showing remarkable vitality and confidence in 2024.

The top 5 Vue projects: Nuxt leads at 6,200 stars, PrimeVue at 5,400, Slidev at 4,700, shadcn-vue at 4,100, and VitePress at 3,700.

Two notable trends here. First, shadcn-vue's presence at #4 — the port of shadcn/ui's component ownership model to Vue — demonstrates that the copy-paste paradigm is framework-agnostic.

Second, the flourishing of high-quality UI libraries like PrimeVue and the active development in Nuxt (as highlighted by core team lead Daniel Roe) signals growing ecosystem confidence.

Vue 3.5 brought a reactivity system rework with the lighter alien-signals approach already landing in the main branch — a sign of ongoing technical innovation.

Key points: (1) Nuxt leads Vue ecosystem at 6.2k stars (2) shadcn-vue shows component ownership model is framework-agnostic (3) Vue 3.5 reactivity overhaul signals active development

Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 07_emerging-themes

[Transition] Beyond the headline numbers, three cross-cutting themes emerged in 2024 that will shape the ecosystem's future.

First: AI-powered projects dominated like never before. n8n led the charge at 17,000 stars with native AI workflow automation, followed by Flowise at 14,500 for visual LLM flow building, and AFFiNE combining knowledge management with AI. Supabase's AI features added another 14,500 stars.

Second: Tauri continued its push for lighter desktop apps at 15,900 stars. Compared to typical Electron apps, Tauri binaries are roughly 10x smaller — a compelling argument for cross-platform desktop development.

Third: Browser-based innovation showcased what's possible when WebAssembly unlocks new capabilities. PGlite runs Postgres entirely in the browser via WASM, and WebVM runs a complete virtual machine in-browser.

The BaaS (Backend-as-a-Service) trend, exemplified by Supabase's 14,500 stars, continues to abstract away backend complexity for frontend developers.

Key points: (1) AI projects dominated: n8n, Flowise, AFFiNE, Supabase all in top 10 (2) Tauri enables 10x smaller desktop apps (3) Browser innovation with PGlite and WebVM pushing web boundaries

Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 08_takeaways

[Transition] Let's distill what 2024 tells us about JavaScript's trajectory and what it means for 2025.

Five actionable takeaways:

First, component ownership beats imports. shadcn/ui's copy-paste model proved its staying power for the second consecutive year, reaching 77,500 total stars. Developers want control over their component code, not npm-installed black boxes.

Second, HTML-first approaches gained serious traction. htmx overtaking React validates the server-driven, low-JavaScript architecture movement. Not every project needs a SPA framework.

Third, React is becoming a framework specification. With Server Components and Server Functions, the line between React library and React framework is blurring. Multiple frameworks now implement React's primitives differently.

Fourth, AI integration is table stakes. Four of the top 10 projects have significant AI capabilities. In 2025, having AI features won't differentiate your project — not having them will be a liability.

Fifth, Vue's UI library ecosystem signals maturity. The wave of high-quality libraries like PrimeVue and shadcn-vue, combined with Vue 3.5's reactivity overhaul, shows a confident, maturing ecosystem.

Looking ahead to 2025: expect more frameworks to adopt Server Components, AI-first projects will continue surging, and the component ownership model will spawn even more derivative libraries.

Key points: (1) Component ownership model wins — shadcn/ui back-to-back champion (2) htmx validates HTML-first approach (3) AI integration is now baseline expectation (4) React becoming specification, not library (5) Vue ecosystem shows maturity

Duration: 2 minutes

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720" width="1280" height="720">
    <defs>
        <linearGradient id="bgGrad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="100%">
            <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#0D1117"/>
            <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#161B22"/>
        </linearGradient>
        <linearGradient id="cardGrad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="0%" y2="100%">
            <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#21262D"/>
            <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#161B22"/>
        </linearGradient>
        <linearGradient id="aiGrad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="100%">
            <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#A855F7"/>
            <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#7C3AED"/>
        </linearGradient>
        <linearGradient id="desktopGrad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="100%">
            <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#58A6FF"/>
            <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#388BFD"/>
        </linearGradient>
        <linearGradient id="backendGrad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="100%">
            <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#7EE787"/>
            <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#22C55E"/>
        </linearGradient>
        <filter id="cardShadow">
            <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="4"/>
            <feOffset dx="0" dy="2"/>
            <feComponentTransfer>
                <feFuncA type="linear" slope="0.2"/>
            </feComponentTransfer>
            <feMerge>
                <feMergeNode/>
                <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
            </feMerge>
        </filter>
    </defs>

    <!-- Background -->
    <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#bgGrad)"/>

    <!-- Title area -->
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="120" fill="#161B22"/>
    <rect x="60" y="50" width="6" height="40" rx="3" fill="#A855F7"/>
    <text x="80" y="75" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="700" fill="#E6EDF3">
        <tspan>Emerging Themes: AI, Desktop, and Browser Innovation</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="80" y="100" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#8B949E">
        <tspan>Cross-cutting trends reshaping the JavaScript landscape in 2024</tspan>
    </text>

    <!-- Three theme cards -->
    <!-- Card 1: AI Projects -->
    <rect x="60" y="160" width="370" height="380" rx="12" fill="url(#cardGrad)" filter="url(#cardShadow)"/>
    <rect x="60" y="160" width="370" height="8" rx="4" fill="url(#aiGrad)"/>

    <!-- AI icon placeholder -->
    <circle cx="110" cy="230" r="28" fill="#A855F7" fill-opacity="0.2"/>
    <text x="110" y="238" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle">🤖</text>

    <text x="160" y="220" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="700" fill="#E6EDF3">AI-Powered Projects</text>
    <text x="90" y="260" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#8B949E">
        <tspan>AI integration dominates the ecosystem</tspan>
    </text>

    <!-- AI project list -->
    <g>
        <rect x="90" y="295" width="8" height="8" rx="4" fill="#A855F7"/>
        <text x="115" y="305" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#E6EDF3">n8n</text>
        <text x="280" y="305" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#A855F7">+17.0k</text>
    </g>
    <text x="115" y="330" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#6E7681">
        <tspan>Workflow automation with native AI</tspan>
    </text>

    <g>
        <rect x="90" y="365" width="8" height="8" rx="4" fill="#A855F7"/>
        <text x="115" y="375" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#E6EDF3">Flowise</text>
        <text x="280" y="375" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#A855F7">+14.5k</text>
    </g>
    <text x="115" y="400" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#6E7681">
        <tspan>Drag & drop UI for custom LLM flows</tspan>
    </text>

    <g>
        <rect x="90" y="435" width="8" height="8" rx="4" fill="#A855F7"/>
        <text x="115" y="445" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#E6EDF3">AFFiNE</text>
        <text x="280" y="445" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#A855F7">+19.6k</text>
    </g>
    <text x="115" y="470" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#6E7681">
        <tspan>Knowledge base with AI capabilities</tspan>
    </text>

    <g>
        <rect x="90" y="505" width="8" height="8" rx="4" fill="#A855F7"/>
        <text x="115" y="515" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#E6EDF3">Supabase</text>
        <text x="280" y="515" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#A855F7">+14.5k</text>
    </g>
    <text x="115" y="540" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#6E7681">
        <tspan>Open-source Firebase alternative + AI</tspan>
    </text>

    <!-- Card 2: Desktop -->
    <rect x="455" y="160" width="370" height="380" rx="12" fill="url(#cardGrad)" filter="url(#cardShadow)"/>
    <rect x="455" y="160" width="370" height="8" rx="4" fill="url(#desktopGrad)"/>

    <!-- Desktop icon -->
    <circle cx="505" cy="230" r="28" fill="#58A6FF" fill-opacity="0.2"/>
    <text x="505" y="238" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle">🖥️</text>

    <text x="555" y="220" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="700" fill="#E6EDF3">Desktop & Mobile</text>
    <text x="485" y="260" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#8B949E">
        <tspan>Lighter apps with web technologies</tspan>
    </text>

    <!-- Tauri -->
    <g>
        <rect x="485" y="295" width="8" height="8" rx="4" fill="#58A6FF"/>
        <text x="510" y="305" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#E6EDF3">Tauri</text>
        <text x="680" y="305" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#58A6FF">+15.9k ★</text>
    </g>
    <text x="510" y="330" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#6E7681">
        <tspan>Build smaller, faster desktop apps</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="510" y="350" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#6E7681">
        <tspan>with your favorite web framework</tspan>
    </text>

    <!-- Desktop stats -->
    <rect x="485" y="400" width="310" height="100" rx="8" fill="#161B22"/>
    <text x="510" y="435" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#8B949E">
        <tspan>Tauri vs Electron</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="510" y="470" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="700" fill="#58A6FF">
        <tspan>~10x smaller</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="510" y="495" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#6E7681">
        <tspan>Binary size vs typical Electron app</tspan>
    </text>

    <!-- Card 3: Browser Innovation -->
    <rect x="850" y="160" width="370" height="380" rx="12" fill="url(#cardGrad)" filter="url(#cardShadow)"/>
    <rect x="850" y="160" width="370" height="8" rx="4" fill="url(#backendGrad)"/>

    <!-- Browser icon -->
    <circle cx="900" cy="230" r="28" fill="#7EE787" fill-opacity="0.2"/>
    <text x="900" y="238" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle">🌐</text>

    <text x="950" y="220" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="700" fill="#E6EDF3">Browser Innovation</text>
    <text x="880" y="260" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#8B949E">
        <tspan>Pushing the boundaries of the web</tspan>
    </text>

    <!-- PGlite -->
    <g>
        <rect x="880" y="295" width="8" height="8" rx="4" fill="#7EE787"/>
        <text x="905" y="305" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#E6EDF3">PGlite</text>
    </g>
    <text x="905" y="330" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#6E7681">
        <tspan>Postgres running in the browser</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="905" y="350" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#6E7681">
        <tspan>via WebAssembly</tspan>
    </text>

    <!-- WebVM -->
    <g>
        <rect x="880" y="385" width="8" height="8" rx="4" fill="#7EE787"/>
        <text x="905" y="395" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#E6EDF3">WebVM</text>
    </g>
    <text x="905" y="420" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#6E7681">
        <tspan>Virtual machine running</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="905" y="440" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#6E7681">
        <tspan>entirely in the browser</tspan>
    </text>

    <!-- BaaS trend -->
    <rect x="880" y="480" width="310" height="40" rx="6" fill="#7EE787" fill-opacity="0.15"/>
    <text x="1035" y="505" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="600" fill="#7EE787" text-anchor="middle">BaaS Trend: Supabase +14.5k</text>

    <!-- Footer -->
    <text x="60" y="690" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#6E7681">
        <tspan>Source: risingstars.js.org/2024</tspan>
    </text>
</svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720" width="1280" height="720">
    <defs>
        <linearGradient id="bgGrad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="100%">
            <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#0D1117"/>
            <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#161B22"/>
        </linearGradient>
        <linearGradient id="cardGrad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="0%" y2="100%">
            <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#21262D"/>
            <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#161B22"/>
        </linearGradient>
        <linearGradient id="aiGrad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="100%">
            <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#A855F7"/>
            <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#7C3AED"/>
        </linearGradient>
        <linearGradient id="desktopGrad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="100%">
            <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#58A6FF"/>
            <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#388BFD"/>
        </linearGradient>
        <linearGradient id="backendGrad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="100%">
            <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#7EE787"/>
            <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#22C55E"/>
        </linearGradient>
        <filter id="cardShadow">
            <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="4"/>
            <feOffset dx="0" dy="2"/>
            <feComponentTransfer>
                <feFuncA type="linear" slope="0.2"/>
            </feComponentTransfer>
            <feMerge>
                <feMergeNode/>
                <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
            </feMerge>
        </filter>
    </defs>

    <!-- Background -->
    <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#bgGrad)"/>

    <!-- Title area -->
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="120" fill="#161B22"/>
    <rect x="60" y="50" width="6" height="40" rx="3" fill="#A855F7"/>
    <text x="80" y="75" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="700" fill="#E6EDF3">
        <tspan>Emerging Themes: AI, Desktop, and Browser Innovation</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="80" y="100" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#8B949E">
        <tspan>Cross-cutting trends reshaping the JavaScript landscape in 2024</tspan>
    </text>

    <!-- Three theme cards -->
    <!-- Card 1: AI Projects -->
    <rect x="60" y="160" width="370" height="380" rx="12" fill="url(#cardGrad)" filter="url(#cardShadow)"/>
    <rect x="60" y="160" width="370" height="8" rx="4" fill="url(#aiGrad)"/>

    <!-- AI icon placeholder -->
    <circle cx="110" cy="230" r="28" fill="#A855F7" fill-opacity="0.2"/>
    <text x="110" y="238" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle">🤖</text>

    <text x="160" y="220" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="700" fill="#E6EDF3">AI-Powered Projects</text>
    <text x="90" y="260" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#8B949E">
        <tspan>AI integration dominates the ecosystem</tspan>
    </text>

    <!-- AI project list -->
    <g>
        <rect x="90" y="295" width="8" height="8" rx="4" fill="#A855F7"/>
        <text x="115" y="305" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#E6EDF3">n8n</text>
        <text x="280" y="305" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#A855F7">+17.0k</text>
    </g>
    <text x="115" y="330" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#6E7681">
        <tspan>Workflow automation with native AI</tspan>
    </text>

    <g>
        <rect x="90" y="365" width="8" height="8" rx="4" fill="#A855F7"/>
        <text x="115" y="375" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#E6EDF3">Flowise</text>
        <text x="280" y="375" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#A855F7">+14.5k</text>
    </g>
    <text x="115" y="400" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#6E7681">
        <tspan>Drag & drop UI for custom LLM flows</tspan>
    </text>

    <g>
        <rect x="90" y="435" width="8" height="8" rx="4" fill="#A855F7"/>
        <text x="115" y="445" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#E6EDF3">AFFiNE</text>
        <text x="280" y="445" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#A855F7">+19.6k</text>
    </g>
    <text x="115" y="470" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#6E7681">
        <tspan>Knowledge base with AI capabilities</tspan>
    </text>

    <g>
        <rect x="90" y="505" width="8" height="8" rx="4" fill="#A855F7"/>
        <text x="115" y="515" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#E6EDF3">Supabase</text>
        <text x="280" y="515" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#A855F7">+14.5k</text>
    </g>
    <text x="115" y="540" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#6E7681">
        <tspan>Open-source Firebase alternative + AI</tspan>
    </text>

    <!-- Card 2: Desktop -->
    <rect x="455" y="160" width="370" height="380" rx="12" fill="url(#cardGrad)" filter="url(#cardShadow)"/>
    <rect x="455" y="160" width="370" height="8" rx="4" fill="url(#desktopGrad)"/>

    <!-- Desktop icon -->
    <circle cx="505" cy="230" r="28" fill="#58A6FF" fill-opacity="0.2"/>
    <text x="505" y="238" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle">🖥️</text>

    <text x="555" y="220" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="700" fill="#E6EDF3">Desktop & Mobile</text>
    <text x="485" y="260" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#8B949E">
        <tspan>Lighter apps with web technologies</tspan>
    </text>

    <!-- Tauri -->
    <g>
        <rect x="485" y="295" width="8" height="8" rx="4" fill="#58A6FF"/>
        <text x="510" y="305" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#E6EDF3">Tauri</text>
        <text x="680" y="305" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#58A6FF">+15.9k ★</text>
    </g>
    <text x="510" y="330" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#6E7681">
        <tspan>Build smaller, faster desktop apps</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="510" y="350" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#6E7681">
        <tspan>with your favorite web framework</tspan>
    </text>

    <!-- Desktop stats -->
    <rect x="485" y="400" width="310" height="100" rx="8" fill="#161B22"/>
    <text x="510" y="435" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#8B949E">
        <tspan>Tauri vs Electron</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="510" y="470" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="700" fill="#58A6FF">
        <tspan>~10x smaller</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="510" y="495" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#6E7681">
        <tspan>Binary size vs typical Electron app</tspan>
    </text>

    <!-- Card 3: Browser Innovation -->
    <rect x="850" y="160" width="370" height="380" rx="12" fill="url(#cardGrad)" filter="url(#cardShadow)"/>
    <rect x="850" y="160" width="370" height="8" rx="4" fill="url(#backendGrad)"/>

    <!-- Browser icon -->
    <circle cx="900" cy="230" r="28" fill="#7EE787" fill-opacity="0.2"/>
    <text x="900" y="238" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle">🌐</text>

    <text x="950" y="220" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="700" fill="#E6EDF3">Browser Innovation</text>
    <text x="880" y="260" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#8B949E">
        <tspan>Pushing the boundaries of the web</tspan>
    </text>

    <!-- PGlite -->
    <g>
        <rect x="880" y="295" width="8" height="8" rx="4" fill="#7EE787"/>
        <text x="905" y="305" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#E6EDF3">PGlite</text>
    </g>
    <text x="905" y="330" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#6E7681">
        <tspan>Postgres running in the browser</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="905" y="350" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#6E7681">
        <tspan>via WebAssembly</tspan>
    </text>

    <!-- WebVM -->
    <g>
        <rect x="880" y="385" width="8" height="8" rx="4" fill="#7EE787"/>
        <text x="905" y="395" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#E6EDF3">WebVM</text>
    </g>
    <text x="905" y="420" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#6E7681">
        <tspan>Virtual machine running</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="905" y="440" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#6E7681">
        <tspan>entirely in the browser</tspan>
    </text>

    <!-- BaaS trend -->
    <rect x="880" y="480" width="310" height="40" rx="6" fill="#7EE787" fill-opacity="0.15"/>
    <text x="1035" y="505" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="600" fill="#7EE787" text-anchor="middle">BaaS Trend: Supabase +14.5k</text>

    <!-- Footer -->
    <text x="60" y="690" font-family="Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#6E7681">
        <tspan>Source: risingstars.js.org/2024</tspan>
    </text>
</svg>
